learn.title: Strategy guide
learn.subtitle: How each strategy works, which market it suits, and where it hurts. Read this before you switch any of them on with real money.
learn.strategies_hint: Tap a card to see how it trades, when it works, and its default settings.
learn.disclaimer.title: Risk warning
learn.disclaimer.body: No strategy wins all the time. Crypto is highly volatile and leveraged trading can wipe out your entire balance. These defaults were tuned on past data, not on the future. Only trade money you can afford to lose.
learn.basic.risk.title: Risk management
learn.basic.risk.body: The bot risks only a fixed share of your balance per trade (1% by default). Position size is derived from the stop-loss distance rather than a fixed amount — the wider the stop, the smaller the size, so the risk stays constant. Leverage only reduces the margin required; it does not change per-trade risk, but it does raise liquidation risk.
learn.basic.sltp.title: ATR-based stop-loss and take-profit
learn.basic.sltp.body: ATR measures the market's average trading range. Instead of a fixed percentage, stop-loss and take-profit are built from a multiple of ATR — automatically wider in volatile markets and tighter in calm ones. Both are placed at the same distance, so the risk-to-reward ratio is 1:1.
learn.basic.paper.title: Paper vs live
learn.basic.paper.body: Paper mode trades with simulated money but real market prices, so the strategy behaves realistically with nothing at stake. Run every strategy in paper mode for a few weeks first. Live trading requires an active token.
learn.basic.backtest.title: Backtesting
learn.basic.backtest.body: The backtest replays the strategy over historical candles using the same stop-loss and take-profit logic as the live bot, with exchange fees deducted. Past results never guarantee future ones — but a strategy that lost money in the past is almost never worth real risk.

learn.s.supertrend_ema_rsi.goal: Catch a trend as it starts and stay in it until it reverses
learn.s.supertrend_ema_rsi.how1: SuperTrend defines the trend direction; each time its line flips from one side of price to the other, the trend has changed.
learn.s.supertrend_ema_rsi.how2: A long EMA acts as a filter: buy only while price is above it, sell only while price is below it.
learn.s.supertrend_ema_rsi.how3: RSI gives the final confirmation (above 50 to buy, below 50 to sell). A signal fires only on the bar SuperTrend flips, not on every bar.
learn.s.supertrend_ema_rsi.best: Trending markets with sustained moves. In a range, SuperTrend flips constantly and produces one false signal after another.
learn.s.supertrend_ema_rsi.tip: Do not lower the SuperTrend multiplier; a smaller number means more sensitivity and more whipsaw. If you get too many trades, raise it instead.
learn.s.macd_trend.goal: Ride momentum in the direction of the main trend
learn.s.macd_trend.how1: The MACD histogram shows the gap between short-term and long-term price momentum.
learn.s.macd_trend.how2: The histogram crossing zero upward is a buy signal; crossing zero downward is a sell signal.
learn.s.macd_trend.how3: A trend EMA filters entries: buy only above it, sell only below it. This removes most counter-trend signals.
learn.s.macd_trend.best: Medium-term trends with regular pullbacks. The 1-hour timeframe and above is more stable.
learn.s.macd_trend.tip: MACD lags by design. If you want early entries this is the wrong strategy; its strength is staying with long trends.
learn.s.bollinger_rsi.goal: Buy the bottom of the range and sell the top, while the market is range-bound
learn.s.bollinger_rsi.how1: Bollinger Bands plot two standard deviations above and below a 20-bar average — the 'normal' range of movement.
learn.s.bollinger_rsi.how2: When price pierces the lower band and then closes back inside it, that is a buy signal; the mirror case is a sell.
learn.s.bollinger_rsi.how3: RSI must be in its extreme zone at the same time. A bounce without an RSI extreme is ignored.
learn.s.bollinger_rsi.best: A market with no clear trend, oscillating around an average.
learn.s.bollinger_rsi.tip: In a strong trend price can 'walk the band' for a long time and this strategy loses repeatedly. Turn it off in those conditions or move to a higher timeframe.
learn.s.ma_kijun_psar.goal: Require multiple layers of trend confirmation before entering
learn.s.ma_kijun_psar.how1: Three moving averages (fast, mid, slow) must line up in order, forming a bullish or bearish ribbon.
learn.s.ma_kijun_psar.how2: Kijun — the midpoint of the 26-bar high and low — acts as the equilibrium line, and price must be on the correct side of it.
learn.s.ma_kijun_psar.how3: PSAR gives the final directional confirmation. A signal fires only on the bar the ribbon *forms*, not for as long as it holds.
learn.s.ma_kijun_psar.best: Fresh, sustained trends. This is the strictest strategy here and produces the fewest signals.
learn.s.ma_kijun_psar.tip: Because three filters must agree, it can go weeks without a signal in a quiet market. That is not a fault, it is the design — quality over quantity.
learn.s.donchian_breakout.goal: Profit from breaks of support and resistance levels
learn.s.donchian_breakout.how1: The highest high and lowest low of the last N bars are treated as resistance and support (a Donchian channel).
learn.s.donchian_breakout.how2: A breakout counts only when a bar *closes* beyond the level — not merely touches it. An ATR margin makes the bot ignore breaks of just a few ticks.
learn.s.donchian_breakout.how3: Volume on that bar must exceed the average. A breakout on thin volume is usually false and price falls back inside the channel.
learn.s.donchian_breakout.best: Volatile markets, and the moment price escapes a period of consolidation.
learn.s.donchian_breakout.tip: Fakeouts are this strategy's most common trap. If you hit a run of losses, raise the volume multiplier and the ATR margin to make it stricter.
learn.s.rsi_contrarian.goal: Buy the bottom and sell the top — deliberately trading against the short-term move
learn.s.rsi_contrarian.how1: RSI marks the oversold and overbought zones; both thresholds are configurable (25 and 75 by default).
learn.s.rsi_contrarian.how2: Entry happens as RSI *leaves* the extreme zone, not as it enters. RSI can stay oversold for days, and buying at that moment is catching a falling knife.
learn.s.rsi_contrarian.how3: An ADX filter is also available: if ADX is above the threshold the trend is strong and no trade is taken. The default is 100, which effectively disables it — in our tests tightening this filter cut the number of signals so far that results got worse, not better. Set it to 25 if you want to trade only in ranging markets.
learn.s.rsi_contrarian.best: Range-bound, trendless markets — exactly where trend-following strategies bleed.
learn.s.rsi_contrarian.tip: This is the riskiest strategy here because it enters against the current move on purpose. Never remove the stop-loss, and start with small size.
learn.s.volatility_shock.goal: Profit from sudden jumps, which usually follow an important news event
learn.s.volatility_shock.how1: The bot has no news feed; instead it detects the footprint news leaves in the market itself.
learn.s.volatility_shock.how2: Three conditions must hold at once: volume several times the average, a candle range several times ATR, and a large body relative to the wicks (a decisive move, not hesitation).
learn.s.volatility_shock.how3: Entry goes in the direction of that impulse candle: a bullish candle buys, a bearish one sells.
learn.s.volatility_shock.best: Moments when major news breaks — regulatory changes, network upgrades, or statements by influential figures.
learn.s.volatility_shock.tip: For genuinely news-driven, well-timed trades the TradingView webhook fits better: you decide and the bot only executes. This strategy does not replace following the news, it only captures the market's reaction.
learn.s.hybrid_trend_breakout.goal: Combine trend detection with a breakout entry
learn.s.hybrid_trend_breakout.how1: The trend is set by two EMAs (fast and slow), and ADX measures how strong it is.
learn.s.hybrid_trend_breakout.how2: If the trend is not strong enough — a low ADX — no trade is taken at all, even when a breakout happens.
learn.s.hybrid_trend_breakout.how3: Entry comes only from a channel breakout, and only in the direction of that main trend; counter-trend breakouts are ignored.
learn.s.hybrid_trend_breakout.best: Strong trends that climb (or fall) in steps with short pullbacks.
learn.s.hybrid_trend_breakout.tip: Three simultaneous filters mean fewer but higher-quality signals. If you want more signals, lower ADX first rather than the volume multiplier.
strategy.adaptive_regime.label: Automatic: pick the strategy from market conditions
strategy.param.enable_shock: React to news shocks (1 = on, 0 = off)
learn.s.adaptive_regime.goal: Instead of you choosing the strategy, the system detects the market type and runs the strategy that suits it
learn.s.adaptive_regime.how1: ADX measures trend strength and classifies the market: above the trending threshold → trending market; below the ranging threshold → ranging market.
learn.s.adaptive_regime.how2: Based on that class the work is delegated: trending → SuperTrend + EMA + RSI; ranging → Contrarian (RSI); and a sudden volume and range spike → News shock reaction, which takes priority over both.
learn.s.adaptive_regime.how3: Between the two thresholds there is a *dead band* where no trade is taken. This is deliberate: with a single threshold, ADX oscillating around that number would make the bot flip between two opposite logics every few bars.
learn.s.adaptive_regime.best: When you do not know whether the market ahead will trend or range, or when you do not want to switch strategies by hand. It helps most on a symbol or timeframe whose behaviour keeps changing.
learn.s.adaptive_regime.tip: This is not magic, and we report its measurement honestly. Across 18 real datasets the automatic mode beat the trend strategy it replaces (median −0.86% → +0.04%), but it did not beat the best fixed strategy on that same data (Contrarian, +0.84%). The reason is plain: that period was mostly ranging, so in hindsight a pure range strategy wins. Automatic mode earns its keep when you do *not* know in advance what the market ahead looks like — it is insurance against running the wrong strategy, not a profit multiplier. Note too that regime detection lags by nature, since ADX is computed from past data.
learn.bt.title: Test results and methodology
learn.bt.intro: Each strategy's defaults are not guesses; they were tested on real market data. This section states exactly what was run, what came out, and what turned out contrary to expectation — including the parts that reflect badly on the strategies themselves.
learn.bt.method1: 18 real datasets from the Toobit exchange: 6 symbols (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB) × 3 timeframes (15m, 1h, 4h), about 1000 candles each.
learn.bt.method2: The same stop-loss and take-profit logic as the live bot: symmetric and ATR-based, at a 1:1 risk-to-reward ratio.
learn.bt.method3: The exchange's taker fee is deducted on both entry and exit. Without it every strategy looks misleadingly better than it is.
learn.bt.method4: Risk per trade is 1% of current equity, exactly like the bot's default setting.
learn.bt.method5: The first 210 candles of each dataset were used only to warm up the indicators; no trade is recorded in that span.
learn.bt.method6: Dozens of parameter combinations were tried per strategy, and the winning combination became that strategy's default.
learn.bt.metric_note: The selection metric was deliberately not 'highest return'. Choosing by highest return means gluing the parameters to this particular data (overfitting), which usually fails in a live market. Our metric was the median return across all 18 datasets plus the share of datasets that were profitable — that favours a strategy which is acceptable in most markets over one that is brilliant in a single market and a disaster everywhere else.
learn.bt.table_title: Result of each strategy with its current defaults
learn.bt.table_sub: Aggregated over all 18 datasets, fees deducted. Sorted by median return.
learn.bt.finding1_title: Most strategies were negative over this window
learn.bt.finding1_body: Only four of nine strategies had a positive median, and all by a small margin. We are not hiding this, because it says something important about automated trading: the window tested was mostly range-bound, so trend strategies naturally lost. Test a different window and the order of this table would likely change.
learn.bt.finding2_title: A filter meant to help was doing harm
learn.bt.finding2_body: The original design made the ADX filter mandatory for the Contrarian strategy, reasoning that counter-trend trades belong only in ranging markets. The test said otherwise: tightening that filter cut the signal count so far that results got worse. So its default now leaves it effectively off, and the guide states that fact instead of repeating the original reasoning.
learn.bt.finding3_title: A bigger risk-to-reward ratio did not rescue the breakout strategies
learn.bt.finding3_body: Breakout win rates ran around 45%, and at equal reward-to-risk such a rate loses money after fees. So the reasonable hypothesis was that a farther take-profit would fix it. It was tested: at 1:1.5 the breakout strategy improved from -1.91% to -1.05% but stayed negative, and the hybrid strategy got worse. With insufficient evidence, the engine's logic was left untouched.
learn.bt.finding4_body: The backtest reserved only 60 candles to warm up indicators, while several strategies use a 200-period EMA. The first signals of every backtest were therefore taken on an average that had not converged, so results did not match the live bot (which loads 500 candles). It was raised to 210, and every number in this table was produced after that fix.
learn.bt.caveat_title: What this table does not prove
learn.bt.caveat_body: This is a snapshot of one specific market window, not a forecast. Past performance guarantees nothing about the future, and the window tested particularly favoured mean-reversion strategies and punished trend strategies. Treat the numbers as a relative comparison between strategies, not as an expected return. Always backtest on your own symbols and timeframes, and run in paper mode first.

set.2fa_off: Not enabled yet. Until you turn this on, no account can be switched to live trading.
set.2fa_step1: Open Google Authenticator (or Authy, 1Password, or similar).
set.2fa_step2: Scan the QR code below, or type the key in manually.
set.2fa_step3: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows to turn it on.
set.2fa_no_qr: The QR code did not load — use the text key below instead.
set.2fa_recovery_desc: If you lose your phone, these are the only way back in. Each works once, and this is the only time they are shown.
set.2fa_disable_warn: Disabling this returns all of your live accounts to paper mode.
set.2fa_disable_confirm: Disabling two-factor authentication returns all of your live accounts to paper mode. Continue?
set.2fa_reverted: Two-factor authentication disabled, and these accounts returned to paper mode: {names}
